name: PhotoCraft
summary: Edit photos and Photoshop files in Nextcloud with PhotoCraft
description:
Open a photo or a layered image in Files with **Edit in PhotoCraft** and work on it right in the browser: layers, masks, adjustment layers, selections, brushes, retouching, filters and text, with Photoshop (PSD, PSB) files as well as PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, HEIC and camera raw files.

- **Save** writes a layered file (PSD, PSB, PhotoCraft) straight back to Nextcloud, which keeps the previous state as a file version. A flat image that gained layers asks for a name and folder first, as in Photoshop.
- **Save As** and **Export** store a file in any folder you pick.
- Read-only files open normally; saving offers a copy.
- If someone else changes the file while you have it open, you choose whether to replace their version or save a copy.
- Optionally, clicking an image in Files opens it in PhotoCraft instead of the viewer.
readme_features:
- **Edit in PhotoCraft** appears in the Files action menu of every image PhotoCraft opens: PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP, HEIC, camera raw, Photoshop (PSD, PSB), OpenRaster, Paint.NET and PhotoCraft files.
- **Save** (Ctrl/⌘+S) writes a layered file (PSD, PSB, PhotoCraft) back to Nextcloud, and Nextcloud keeps the previous state as a file version. A flat image that gained layers asks for a name and folder first, as Photoshop does.
- **Save As** and **Export** ask for a name and folder in your Nextcloud.
readme_limitations: - Brush, gradient and swatch libraries stay in the browser's storage, as in PhotoCraft's own web version.
bridge_notes: With `?host=parent`, Save, Save As and Export ask the parent where to save (`photocraft:pick-save`), what PhotoCraft writes goes to the parent instead of the browser's downloads, and the parent (not PhotoCraft) guards leaving the page with unsaved changes. File › Open keeps the browser's own file picker.
